title: Dedicated/Private Observability: VPC & On‑Prem Collectors + Tenant Isolation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver production-grade observability for Dedicated and Private deployments by building a secure, configurable collector model for VPC/on‑prem environments and guaranteeing per-tenant isolation at ingestion, storage, and dashboarding. This work covers: (1) an embeddable collector binary/agent that customers can deploy in their VPC or on-prem cluster; (2) secure forward path (mTLS / signed JWT) to our ingestion plane or to customer-managed backends; (3) tenant-aware ingestion pipelines (traces, metrics, logs) that enforce namespace isolation and access controls; (4) per-tenant latency/error dashboards and SLO tooling integrated into Redwood Console.
acceptance_criteria: Collector agent (redwood-collector v1) can be deployed as a DaemonSet/Service on customer k8s and as a systemd service on Linux hosts
Agent supports OpenTelemetry OTLP over mTLS and can forward to either Redwood ingestion endpoints or configured external endpoints (Prometheus remote_write, Syslog, SIEM)
All incoming telemetry carries tenant_id and request_id and is stored/tagged such that queries and dashboards are tenant-scoped by default
No cross-tenant queryable metrics/logs/traces in the default console view; RBAC prevents accidental cross-tenant access
Per-tenant latency and error dashboards generated automatically for Dedicated deployments with sample dashboards for top 10 routes and p95/p99 SLOs
End-to-end encryption (in transit) and token/key rotation documented; security review completed and sign-off obtained
Performance: collector adds <5ms median latency per request path for forwarding; ingestion pipeline sustains our committed throughput for Dedicated pool sizes
Canary rollout path exists (config flag + telemetry sampling) and rollback tested end-to-end
tasks: Design collector configuration schema (tls, endpoints, batching, sampling, resource limits)
Implement redwood-collector: OTLP receiver, batching, local caching, backpressure handling
Add mTLS and JWT-based auth modes; integrate with KMS for key rotation docs
Extend ingestion pipeline to validate tenant_id and apply tenant isolation at ingestion and storage
Extend Console to show tenant selector, per-tenant SLO widgets, and error breakdowns by model/route
Create e2e test harness in dedicated staging that deploys collector and simulates noisy tenants
Prepare migration/upgrade guide and helm chart + systemd unit templates
Run security review and threat model; address findings
notes: Trade-offs: pushing processing into the local collector reduces upstream bandwidth and PII exposure, but increases footprint and upgrade surface on customer infra

We evaluated Fluent Bit vs a custom binary. Fluent Bit handled logs well but complicated trace/metrics correlation; decided on a lightweight custom agent that wraps OpenTelemetry collector components for consistent tracing/metrics handling

Isolation model: prefer logical separation (tenant_id tagging + storage partitioning) over separate physical clusters for scaling reasons; however, for high-security customers we will support dedicated ingestion endpoints and isolated storage buckets as an enterprise option
Sampling strategy: default dynamic sampling (client-side + server-side) to preserve headroom for priority traffic; must expose overrides for customer security investigations
Auth: mTLS for managed-forwarding is primary; outbound-only JWT signed by customer's KMS for customer-managed backends
Rollout: start with internal Dedicated staging customers, then pilot with 2 enterprise customers before GA
